t: Paragraph (2) of subsection (b) of section 27 of the Mineral Leasing Act (41 Stat. 448; 30 U.S.C. 184(b)(2)) is amended by striking “fifteen thousand three hundred and sixty acres” and inserting “30,720 acres”.

fable.w: This section only amends an acreage limit in the Mineral Leasing Act by substituting one number for another. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. The only possible temptation is that the Mineral Leasing Act concerns leases with private parties, but applying for or holding a lease is not participation in a federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking “fifteen thousand three hundred and sixty acres” and inserting “30,720 acres”

opus.w: This section only changes the acreage limit in the Mineral Leasing Act from 15,360 to 30,720 acres. It brings no one from outside the federal government into a federal decision: there is no comment period, hearing, consultation, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue. Mentioning a leasing statute does not create any participation process.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The only possible hook is the mention of the Mineral Leasing Act, which governs federal leasing, so a reader might think leasing decisions involve outside parties. That reading fails because the amendment only changes a number in the acreage limit. It creates no comment period, hearing, consultation, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple textual amendment changing a numerical acreage limit in the Mineral Leasing Act. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation with states or tribes, advisory committees, or other forms of participation by non-federal entities. It is a substantive legislative change, not a procedural requirement for outside involvement in decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: Paragraph (2) of subsection (b) of section 27 of the Mineral Leasing Act (41 Stat. 448; 30 U.S.C. 184(b)(2)) is amended by striking “fifteen thousand three hundred and sixty acres” and inserting “30,720 acres”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that changing an acreage limit affects who can lease land, thus involving outside parties. However, the text itself is merely a numerical amendment to a statutory limit. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory committee involving non-federal actors. It is a substantive change to the law, not a procedural requirement for participation.
